newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh T-bill yields to steady or edge up, dealers.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh T-bill yields to steady or edge up, dealers.

text.p: Yields on Kazakh GKO Treasury bills have fallen as low as they can for now, and dealers expect them to remain steady or grow slightly at auctions next week.

Average yields on six-month GKOs fell to 27.76 percent at an auction on Monday from 30.39 percent two weeks ago. Yields on three-month paper went down to 23.06 percent on Tuesday from 24.04 percent last week.
Next Monday the Finance Ministry will hold an auction of three-month Treasury bills offering a total of 650 million tenge of paper.
"I think yields on three-month paper will go up to some 24 percent annual rather than falling further," Oleg Tsurkan, head treasurer at ABN AMRO Bank Kazakhstan, told Reuters.

Tsurkan said that many local banks had already invested large sums in 14- and 28-day notes issued regularly by the National Bank to sterilise the money supply and support the exchange rate of the tenge.
Yields on 14-day notes averaged 29.98 percent at the auction on Thursday. 28-day notes yielded 29.79 percent last week.
"Therefore, investors may now put smaller sums in GKOs than before, and this may push up yields on T-bills," Tsurkan said.

Tsurkan said some investors could try to invest in hard currency operations, in expectation of a fall in the tenge after it stabilised this week due to National Bank note issues and massive purchases of dollars by local banks buying foreign currency for clients.

But dealers say that any rise in yields will only be modest because foreigners investing in Kazakh T-bills and entitled to buy 15-30 percent of each issue have become aggressive and, unlike local banks, accept lower yields.
"Foreigners, who have become very active of late, will agree to any yield," said Denis Fedoseyenko of Kazkommertsbank.
"At the latest GKO auctions, when yields were falling quickly enough, the influence of foreign participants was especially strong," Tsurkan said.
